title: The Outsiders full thoughts:  @Joe Weinberg  #broadway #musicaltheatr...
transcript: Ranking the last 10 Tony-winners for Best Musical — 2024 edition! when I did this last year people got very heated in the comments so I’d just like to remind everybody to take a deep breath this is just my opinion and actually the stakes are quite low the ranking has changed a bit since last year of course Kinky Boots got the boot And the Outsiders is now on the inside of this ranking and maybe some other changes too, stick around to find out one thing that hasn't changed though: still in last place, Moulin Rouge it has its moments for sure but as a big fan of the film I just didn't find it satisfying at all in 9th place and most recently added, the Outsiders which I actually didn't expect to rank this low until it came down to actually doing the ranking the video with my full thoughts is linked in the caption but to summarize I think the show is goodc not great but just didn't leave as much of an impression on me as the rest of the shows on this list in 8th place, and hear me out on this one seriously I have Dear Evan Hansen this one is really complicated for me okay? because the show resonated with me very deeply when I saw it in 2016 and for reasons that I think are a little different from the reasons most people resonated with it and I still think it has elements that are underrated and even widely misunderstood. but after last year's ranking, I revisited the show I thought about it, had conversations with people and started to acknowledge some of the problems that I have maybe been too forgiving of over the years so I have moved it down a bit in the ranking some people might say that it's still too high but give me some credit here, okay? this is a journey, thanks for joining me! next is Kimberly Akimbo I wasn't really on the hype train for this one I suspected that I would have liked the original play more because I just didn't love how they chose to musicalize it But I still found it pretty charming next I have A Strange Loop, this is a show that I have a lot of respect for it's very ambitious in what it's trying to do and say with its use of form the execution didn't totally come together for me but I do appreciate that the show has resonated with a lot of people more than it did with me moving into the top 5 these are all great shows but in place I have a Gentleman's Guide to love and murmur which some people said was too low in my ranking last year well congratulations I moved it up a bit the show was a delightful and genuinely skillful display of comedy in fourth place Hadestown it's great, I love it gorgeous score, brilliant direction, and underrated book I never know where to put Hamilton in rankings because my feelings about it have been kind of weighed down by burnout, overexposure, and some justified discourse but of course it's an extremely impressive artistic achievement and I was obsessed with it too I mean I was there Gandalf I spent seven months listening to an audio slime of this on loop because there wasn't a cast recording yet so yeah Hamilton is great but I'm just a little bit more in love with the top two so my runner up is The Band's Visit which is a gorgeous tender piece of musical theater that makes excellent use of restraint as a storytelling tool in a way that I wish more musicals were brave enough to attempt (not all of them just more of them) And the Tony wins were very well deserved including Best Actor, but you guys aren't ready for that hot take so we're moving on but finally, still in first place I have Fun Home, because what else? it's a masterfully rendered work of art that makes me laugh and sob! and that's my updated ranking so why don't you go ahead and politely tell me your ranking in the comments!
